subject: APAC healthcare addenda & residency — MedAsia questions
messages:
From: Keiko Suzuki <keiko.suzuki@medasia.jp>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 04:12:00 +0000
Subject: APAC healthcare — addenda & residency questions

Hi Aditya,

Thanks for the quick intro earlier this week. MedAsia is evaluating Redwood for a pilot to surface clinical summaries and provider notifications. Before we proceed to a technical PoC, our legal/procurement teams have a few gating questions around contractual terms and data flows for Japan: 

1) Addenda / DPA: We need to understand how Redwood handles healthcare addenda. For US customers you offer a BAA — can Redwood provide an equivalent contractual commitment under Japanese law (or a Japan-specific addendum)?

2) Subprocessors: We require a current inventory of subprocessors and an option to exclude certain non-Japan subprocessors for this account. Can Redwood provide a CSV or table listing the subprocessors and which ones can be excluded?

3) Residency / Private deployment: MedAsia prefers (ideally) data processing to be restricted to Japan or a Japan-managed VPC. Is an on-prem or Japan-VPC private deployment supported? What are the dependencies (network, KMS, HSM)?

4) Evidence: SOC 2, penetration test reports, and documentation of key management capabilities (BYOK, HSM) will be required.

We attached our initial requirements doc to this message (medasia_requirements_v1.docx). Can you confirm what you can provide and a rough timeline for contracting + procurement?

Appreciate it — if useful we can do a 30-minute call next week (JST).

Regards,
Keiko Suzuki
Head of Compliance & Data Governance
MedAsia Health

Attachments: medasia_requirements_v1.docx (docx)
From: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
To: Keiko Suzuki <keiko.suzuki@medasia.jp>
Cc: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>, Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 20 Apr 2027 10:05:00 +0000
Subject: Re: APAC healthcare — addenda & residency questions

Hi Keiko — thanks for the clear list and the requirements doc. Looping in Laura (legal) and Vivek (product/solutions) so we can assemble a short written checklist and the supporting artifacts you requested.

Short answers up front:
- DPA / Addenda: Redwood can execute a DPA and we have a healthcare addendum (BAA) that covers PHI for US entities. For Japan we typically provide a region-specific addendum or equivalent language; Laura will confirm exact wording and whether an explicit "Japan addendum" is required by your counsel.
- Subprocessors: Attaching our current subprocessor inventory (subprocessor_inventory_20270420.csv). We can discuss allowable exclusions; there are some fixed dependencies (CDN, cloud provider control plane) but many infra-level subprocessors can be scoped per-account with Dedicated/Private.
- Residency / Private: We support VPC-like Private deployments and an on-prem package. Dependencies we need to validate: network egress rules, dedicated GPU hosts or partner colo, and KMS options (BYOK or HSM). Vivek — I flagged the KMS/HSM options below.
- Evidence: We can share SOC 2 Type II, recent pentest summary, and a redacted infrastructure diagram.

I attached a concise "option matrix" that maps contractual and deployment choices to implementation effort and typical lead times: redwood_addenda_option_matrix.pdf. I also linked a short dataflow diagram for your team: https://redwood.share/drive/medasia-dataflow.

Next steps I propose:
1) We (Redwood) produce a 1-page checklist addressing your four asks.
2) Kick off a short (30–45m) call with legal + product to align on required wording, subprocessors to exclude, and timeline.
3) If Private/on-prem is required, we prepare a draft SOW and scoping questions.

Keiko — are you available Thursday 22 Apr 11:00–13:00 JST for a working session?

Thanks,
Aditya Rao
Principal Solutions Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: redwood_addenda_option_matrix.pdf (pdf), subprocessor_inventory_20270420.csv (csv)
From: Laura Bennett <laura.bennett@redwood.com>
To: Aditya Rao <aditya.rao@redwood.com>
Cc: Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>, Mina Haddad <mina.haddad@redwood.com>, Priyom Das <priyom.das@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 21 Apr 2027 12:30:00 +0000
Subject: Re: APAC healthcare — addenda & residency questions

Aditya / team — summary of what we should deliver to MedAsia in preparation for procurement. I pulled key items from Aditya's note and the requirements doc.

Actionable checklist (legal / contracts):
- Confirm classification of data (PHI-equivalent elements). If clinical metadata is considered PHI under their local regime, we should propose the healthcare addendum language.
- Draft a Japan addendum clause (if requested): specify scope, data residency commitment (if possible), security controls, audit rights, and subprocessors clause with exclusions.
- Provide current SOC 2 Type II report and redacted pentest summary.
- Provide subprocessor inventory CSV (attached) and a short table of which subprocessors are negotiable vs. non-negotiable (e.g., core cloud provider control-plane).
- Detail KMS options: BYOK with customer-managed keys, supported KMS providers, and HSM support levels. Note any limitations for Private vs Hosted.
- Draft SOW template for on-prem/VPC engagement (work-breakdown, milestones, responsibilities, network & infra pre-reqs). Attached SOW_template.docx for product to populate.

Operational/technical asks for Product (Vivek / Mina / Priyom):
- Confirm supported deployment topologies for Japan (hosted in Japan region, dedicated pool, on-prem) and estimated lead times for each.
- Verify whether we can provide a formal commitment to keep processing within Japan region (for Private) and the technical guardrails needed to enforce it.
- Confirm any subprocessors that are necessarily outside Japan and options for substitution where feasible.
- KMS/BYOK: confirm supported KMS vendors and whether HSM-backed keys are available for Private deployments.

Please keep the language conservative on residency until Product confirms — we can offer "best-effort to keep processing within Japan for Private deployments" and make any stronger residency commitments subject to SOW and technical validation.

Aditya: can you produce the 1-page checklist and attach the requested artifacts to Keiko? I suggest we avoid initial legal language until we know whether MedAsia will require an explicit Japan addendum versus standard DPA + healthcare addendum.

Laura Bennett
Senior Counsel, Contracts & Privacy
Redwood Inference

Attachment: SOW_template.docx (docx)

Aditya / Laura / Vivek — thanks for the thorough responses and the attachments so far. We reviewed the option matrix and the subprocessor inventory. A few clarifications and next steps from MedAsia: 

- Timeline: procurement window opens first week of May. We need a short checklist and a proposed SOW by 05-May to present to our executive procurement committee.
- Subprocessor exclusions: we'll provide a short list of specific subprocessors we want excluded (third-party analytics vendors). Please indicate if Redwood can isolate those exclusions under a Dedicated or Private engagement.
- Residency ask: our preference is Japan-only processing for PHI-equivalent data. If you cannot commit to a bilateral legal instrument for residency, please state the technical guardrails you can enforce (VPC-only, egress block lists, BYOK in Japan KMS).

Could Redwood produce the following by EOD 05-May?
1) 1-page checklist addressing rights, evidence, and residency options.
2) Draft SOW populated with estimated lead times and an initial cost bucket for Private/on-prem.
3) A redlineable clause for subprocessor exclusions and a short note on which subprocessors are considered non-negotiable.

We are available for a working call on Monday 26 Apr 09:00 JST if that helps.

Best regards,
Keiko Suzuki
Head of Compliance & Data Governance
MedAsia Health
